Apple TV (only $6.99/month for Black Friday) is about to debut its next major sci-fi series: Neuromancer. A recent behind-the-scenes piece reveals new details on what could be the streamer’s next Severance or Pluribus-sized hit.

Neuromancer coming to Apple TV in January, here’s what to expect per creators and cast

Apple TV is home to many beloved sci-fi series, most notably Severance and Pluribus. While we await new seasons of those hits, Apple is about to debut its next big sci-fi show: Neuromancer.

Neuromancer debuts Friday, January 22 with two episodes, followed by weekly releases through March 19.

The series was first teased this July, when Apple debuted the trailer at San Diego Comic-Con. It’s rare for the streamer to hype new shows so far in advance, but Neuromancer was an exception.

After months of minimal news on Neuromancer, a recent WIRED story unveiled what to expect via interviews with series creators Graham Roland and JD Dillard and lead actors Callum Turner and Briana Middleton.

Callum Turner teases: “The world will be taken on a wild ride. It’s an epic. It’s Blade Runner; it’s 2001: A Space Odyssey; it’s The Fifth Element.”

Here are some notable tidbits from the story:

  • Adapting famed novel for TV (Roland): “one of the first things we did was go see Bill Gibson up in Vancouver. He took the burden off of us and let us know that he wasn’t expecting a literal translation of his text.”
  • Meeting fan expectations (Turner): “I try not to think about how important it is and focus on my job of playing the scenes in front of me. JD and Graham had William Gibson’s approval, the scripts were brilliant, and the world so detailed and real.”
  • Prioritizing practical shots (Roland): “JD planted a flag and said, ‘As much as we can, we want an in-camera aesthetic. We want to be practical.’ That really drove the decision to go to Japan.”
  • Core series themes (Middleton): “Our show is asking what happens whenever corporations have unchecked power and when a technology is unchecked and there’s no regulations, and our relationship with that technology goes unchecked…I think life gets much, much worse.”

You can read the full piece over at WIRED for more details.

Neuromancer joins other noteworthy Apple TV premieres coming soon like Bad Monkey’s return, a new crime drama with Hugh Laurie, an original comedy series with Elizabeth Banks and Ted Danson, and more.

Do you plan to watch Neuromancer? Let us know in the comments.

Apple TV is only $6.99/month (over 50% off) for Black Friday. The discounted price lasts up to six months, after which it converts to the standard $14.99/month price.
